decisions.claim: B has been reading a book since last night
decisions.reason: A explicitly states 'You've had your nose buried in that book since last night,' directly attributing the reading activity and its duration to B.

decisions.claim: B has a specific book that B is reading
decisions.reason: The definite demonstrative 'that book' presupposes a specific book exists and is associated with B. This is a genuine E1 presupposition from A's utterance.

decisions.claim: B is expected to finish reading the book
decisions.reason: The temporal clause 'when you're finished' presupposes that B will complete reading the book. This is a standard E1 presupposition triggered by 'when.'

decisions.claim: B is reading a specific book
decisions.reason: c4 ('B is reading a specific book') is strictly entailed by c1 ('B has been reading a book since last night') combined with c2 ('B has a specific book'). c1 is the more complete representative of the reading activity; c4 adds no new information beyond c1+c2.

decisions.claim: B has been reading the book since last night
decisions.reason: c5 ('B has been reading the book since last night') is equivalent to c1 ('B has been reading a book since last night'). The definite 'the' vs indefinite 'a' is a minor variation; both are supported by the same evidence and convey the same core claim.

decisions.claim: B has not yet finished reading the book
decisions.reason: 'Can I read it when you're finished?' presupposes B has not yet finished. This is a genuine E1 presupposition distinct from c3 (which asserts B will finish) by asserting the current incomplete state.

decisions.claim: B has knowledge of the book's content
decisions.reason: 'Don't tell me anything about it' presupposes B has knowledge of the book's content sufficient to tell A about it. This is a genuine E1 presupposition from the imperative's structure.

decisions.claim: B is reading a book of a type that A has not encountered in a long time
decisions.reason: A's statement 'I haven't read a book like that' presupposes the book B is reading belongs to a type/genre that A hasn't encountered in a long time. This is an E2 inference about B's book's characteristics, grounded in A's explicit comparison.
